1.why: All seven screens are static card layouts with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs anywhere.

2.why: The current step is highlighted in the sidebar, primary actions are filled blue buttons, and feedback banners are color-coded, though help and activity-log panels add some competing elements.

3.why: Each screen presents one labeled task at the top with a 'Step X of 6' heading, but the page length (help box, log panel below) means some scrolling past secondary content.

4.why: Password rules are displayed as an on-page checklist and all six steps are listed in the sidebar, so little must be memorized, though the user must still retrieve codes from a separate message.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password manager prompt, or autofill option is visible on any screen.

6.why: Completed steps turn green in the progress list and the demo identifier is shown on step 1, but no saved or prefilled personal items (e.g., stored email in the field) are offered.

7.why: Text is mostly short and plain ('Step 1 of 6. Enter the account email or account ID...'), but a few phrases like 'short-lived and single-use' approval are more technical.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the seven screenshots; only success and information banners are shown, so this claim cannot be verified.

9.why: Step 1 explicitly shows a concrete example identifier 'helena.demo@hospital.test' and 'Next:' lines describe what to do, though not every field has an example.

10.why: The choices actually offered (manual code vs. simulated recovery link, reset vs. 'I know my password — sign in') are clearly labeled, but no face-login option exists.

11.why: Each step has a single primary action, with secondary buttons (Pause, Resume, Back, Show reminder) visually de-emphasized as outlines.

12.why: Every action produces an explicit outcome banner, e.g. 'a secure recovery code has been sent', 'New password saved securely', 'Security code confirmed. You are signed in.'

13.why: A 'Help and safe sign-in' panel with a 'Show a short reminder' button and per-step 'Next:' tips appear on every screen.

14.why: 'Back to recovery request', 'Resume recovery', and a safe-reload note on step 4 support going back and retrying, though no explicit error-retry flow is demonstrated.

15.why: All seven screens share the identical header, sidebar progress list, help panel, and activity log with consistent colors and component styling.
